originalTitle: Harvard to pay $53m over theft and sale of human remains from medical school
summary: Cedric Lodge, 58, sentenced in December to eight years in prison for stealing and selling body parts in national scheme
content: Harvard University has agreed to pay a $53m settlement to resolve civil lawsuits stemming from the illegal theft and sale of human remains that had been donated to its medical school for scientific research. A former Harvard medical school morgue manager, Cedric Lodge, 58, was sentenced in December last year to eight years in prison after he had pleaded guilty in May to stealing and selling human body parts in a nationwide scheme. Prosecutors said this had involved the theft and sale of organs, skin, brains and dissected heads from cadavers donated to Harvard from 2018 through at least March 2020. His wife, Denise Lodge, 65, was also sentenced, to 12 months and one day in prison for her role in the black market scheme. Lodge “took the remains without the knowledge or permission of his employer, the donor, or the donor’s family” and transported them to his home in Goffstown, New Hampshire, where he and his wife would ship them to buyers in other states, according to a US justice department statement. “Remains stolen and sold by the Lodges were transported from the morgue in Boston to locations in Salem, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Pennsylvania,” the statement said. “Many of the remains purchased from Lodge were resold for a profit.” Several other defendants also entered guilty pleas in related cases and were sentenced, the justice department added. The Harvard Crimson reported that as part of the settlement, Harvard Medical School will make a statement to claimant families via a live webinar affirming that Lodge’s conduct was “morally reprehensible” and inconsistent with Harvard’s standards, along with a summary of changes made to its Anatomical Gift Program. The school will also establish an annual financial aid scholarship for medical students starting in the 2027-28 academic year, which it said is intended “in appreciation and in honor of all of our anatomical donors”. Affected families began filing lawsuits against Harvard in the summer of 2023, shortly after Lodge was indicted. The suits alleged negligence, breach of fiduciary duty and infliction of emotional distress. In a statement at the time entitled “An abhorrent betrayal”, the Harvard Medical School deans George Daley and Edward Hundert called Lodge’s actions “morally reprehensible”. Daley and the dean for medical education, Bernard S Chang, wrote in an email sent on Monday to Harvard Medical School and Harvard School of Dental Medicine affiliates that the settlement would allow Harvard and the plaintiffs to avoid “prolonged litigation”, according to the Harvard Crimson’s report. “While Lodge’s sentencing concludes the criminal case against him, and the class action settlement agreement when fulfilled would conclude the civil cases, the process of recovering from this painful incident continues,” Daley and Chang wrote. “These events do not reflect the reverence we hold for the altruistic individuals who selflessly donate their bodies to our Anatomical Gift Program. We reaffirm our deep sorrow and empathy for the families of donors who may have been impacted.”
chineseTitle: 哈佛大学因盗窃和出售医学院人体遗骸而支付 5300 万美元
chineseSummary: 塞德里克·洛奇 (Cedric Lodge)，58 岁，因在国家计划中盗窃和出售身体部位，于 12 月被判处八年监禁
chineseContent: 哈佛大学同意支付 5300 万美元的和解金，以解决因非法盗窃和出售捐赠给其医学院用于科学研究的人体遗骸而引发的民事诉讼。 58 岁的哈佛医学院前太平间经理塞德里克·洛奇（Cedric Lodge）于去年 12 月被判处八年监禁，此前他于 5 月承认在全国范围内盗窃和出售人体器官的罪名。检察官表示，这起案件涉及从 2018 年到至少 2020 年 3 月期间盗窃和出售捐赠给哈佛大学的尸体的器官、皮肤、大脑和解剖头部。他的妻子，65 岁的丹尼斯·洛奇 (Denise Lodge) 也因参与黑市计划而被判处 12 个月零 1 天监禁。根据美国司法部的一份声明，洛奇“在其雇主、捐赠者或捐赠者家人不知情或未允许的情况下带走了遗体”，并将它们运到他位于新罕布什尔州戈夫斯敦的家中，在那里他和他的妻子将把它们运送给其他州的买家。声明称：“旅馆盗窃和出售的遗骸已从波士顿太平间运往马萨诸塞州塞勒姆、新罕布什尔州和宾夕法尼亚州的地点。” “许多从洛奇购买的遗骸都被转售以获取利润。”司法部补充说，其他几名被告也在相关案件中认罪并被判刑。 《哈佛深红报》报道称，作为和解协议的一部分，哈佛医学院将通过现场网络研讨会向索赔家庭发表声明，确认洛奇的行为“在道德上应受谴责”并且不符合哈佛的标准，并总结了其解剖捐赠计划的变化。学校还将从202年开始为医学生设立年度经济援助奖学金
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
